Write $n!=3^s m$ with $3\nmid m$. Then $1/n!=3^{-s}\cdot(1/m)$, so $1/n!\in C$ iff $1/m\in C$ (a ternary shift only adds leading zeros).

If $m>1$, the base-$3$ expansion of $1/m$ is purely periodic with minimal period $t=\operatorname{ord}_m(3)$, and
$$\frac1m=\frac{N}{3^t-1},\qquad N=\frac{3^t-1}{m},$$
where the $t$ ternary digits of $N$ (padded with leading zeros) are exactly one period. Hence $1/m\in C$ forces every digit of $N$ to be $0$ or $2$, so $N$ must be **even**.

For $n\ge6$ we have $k:=v_2(m)=v_2(n!)\ge4$. Since $\operatorname{ord}_{2^k}(3)=2^{k-2}$ and for any odd $p\mid m$ one has $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p(3))\le v_2(p-1)<k-2$ (direct check for $n=6,7$; for $n\ge8$ because $k-2>\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$), the $2$-part of $t$ is exactly $2^{k-2}$, i.e. $v_2(t)=k-2$. By LTE, $v_2(3^t-1)=2+v_2(t)=k$, so $v_2(N)=k-k=0$: $N$ is odd, contradiction. Thus no $n\ge6$ works.

Small cases: $1=0.\overline{2}_3\in C$; $1/2=0.\overline{1}_3$, $1/6=0.0\overline{1}_3$, $1/24=0.0\overline{01}_3$ all contain a $1$; and $1/120=0.0\overline{0002}_3\in C$.

Therefore the intersection is $\{1,\,1/120\}$ and the sum is $1+\frac1{120}=\frac{121}{120}$.
